item.title: A spatially explicit dataset of agriculture liming across the contiguous United States
item.description:
A spatially explicit dataset of agriculture liming across the contiguous United States
Samuel Shou-En Tsao, Tim Jesper Suhrhoff, Giuseppe Amatulli, Maya Almaraz, Jonathan Gewirtzman, Beck Woollen, Eric W. Slessarev, James E. Saiers, Christopher T. Reinhard, Shuang Zhang, Noah J. Planavsky, and Peter A. Raymond
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8801–8819, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8801-2026, 2026
We created the first detailed map of how much agricultural lime has been used across the United States from 1930 to 1987. Lime helps improve soil health and crop growth. Our dataset shows that how and where lime is used depends on climate, soil, and farming practices. By using machine learning, we found environmental patterns that help explain these differences, and invites future research linking lime use to soil health, farming, and climate.
